newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish PM Lipponen has nothing new to say on ERM.
newsitem.headline: Finnish PM Lipponen has nothing new to say on ERM.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Friday he had nothing new to say about Finland and Europe's exchange rate mechanism ERM.
"Concerning Finland, I have nothing new to say about ERM," Lipponen told a news conference.
He declined to comment on news that Italy would start talks as soon as possible about bringing the lira back into ERM.
Lipponen held the news conference ahead of his departure for an informal European Union summit of heads of state and government in Dublin on Saturday.

Lipponen's most recent view on ERM, in a September 27 newspaper interview, was that Finland must take a stand this autumn whether a markka-ERM link is considered a criterion for the third phase of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), and whether a link would add credibility to Finland's economic policy.
The Finnish government's outspoken aim is to ensure that Finland will fulfil in 1997 the entry criteria for EMU.
Lipponen has earlier repeatedly said Finland will decide for or against ERM in an unspecified "near future".
